items.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

ctx.x: Yeah. It was, well you know we had been playing like with Cannonball like a little funk and stuff like that, we had been playing several types of music. So when Cannon passed, I started working with Kenny Rankin. And then we were in San Francisco and they called. But you know I was kind of ready for that because I had been playing a lot of that different type of music and stuff.
How did the thing with the Adderleys come about? Did you step in after, was it Louie Hayes?

Yeah. Well what had happened was I was in New York for a while, and I had played with the ‘tet and I’d played with Betty Carter and I had played with Mitchell and Ruff and Sonny Rollins. I had been with Sonny for quite a while. And then in 1960, no 63, I went back home. I was married, in my first marriage, and I was trying to save this marriage, © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -5-
